newsitem.title: USA: Pregnant U.S. soldier tells of sex with superior.
newsitem.headline: Pregnant U.S. soldier tells of sex with superior.

text.p: A woman soldier told graphically on Wednesday how the Army's top enlisted soldier had sex with her when she was nearly eight months pregnant, likely ruining her career and making her feel "like trash."

Sgt. Christine Roy, 25, was speaking on the first day of a hearing to decide whether Gene McKinney, the Sergeant Major of the Army, will be court-martialed on charges of sexual misconduct involving three Army women and a female sailor.
McKinney, 46, the Army's highest ranking enlisted soldier, has denied the host of charges against him in one of the latest chapters of a growing sexual harassment scandal that has rocked the Army.
Testifying under grant of immunity, Roy revealed the most lurid details of how she gave in to months of McKinney's advances and had sex with him even though both of them were married to other people.
"I felt like trash. I felt really used. When I got home I wanted to hide. I wanted to crawl in bed and make it go away. I was humiliated, I was ashamed, I was embarrassed," Roy said.
"It affected my career, it affected my marriage, it affected my life," she added. "I feel that my career is over. My name will be known. My records will be marked. It's changed my life completely."

The official charge alleges McKinney made unwanted sexual advances against four women, bragging of his sexual prowess and forcing himself upon them physically "with intent to gratify his sexual desires".
McKinney, who faces 18 counts of sexual misconduct, adultery and obstruction of justice, told the court at the start of the session he was not being given a fair hearing.

"I think it's absolutely important that the soldiers know that their senior enlisted soldier is going to get a fair and impartial hearing to see if I am going to be court-martialed," McKinney told investigating officer Col. Robert Jarvis, who is overseeing the hearing at Fort McNair Army Base in Washington.
For much of Roy's testimony, McKinney sat impassively, leaning his chin on his hand while his wife Wilhemina listened without showing emotion in the gallery.

After meeting McKinney at an Armed Services golf tournament in 1996, Roy said he offered her a job, which she declined because of her pregnancy. She said he telephoned her several times over the next few months for sexually suggestive phone conversations. She finally agreed to meet him at his official residence.

Roy, a key government witness in the case, said that on that visit on October 30, 1996, when she was nearly eight months pregnant, she was sitting on the couch in McKinney's sun room when he started kissing and fondling her. She felt shocked and intimidated, she testified.

Roy said McKinney pulled down her maternity pants and they had sexual intercourse while one of her arms was pinned beneath her. Asked why she did not resist, she said: "I felt it was easier just to do it and be over with it."

Asked why, in the telephone calls, she had not simply told McKinney to leave her alone, she said: "This was the Sergeant Major of the Army. You just don't end a conversation with the Sergeant Major of the Army. He achieved something that every enlisted soldier dreams. The mentorship he could have given me was enormous, I didn't want to jeopardise that."
The case against McKinney started when another alleged victim reported his unwanted advances to superiors after learning that he had been named to a top army panel on sexual harassment.
